title: The Last Verdict
premise: Sebastian Winterbourne, the reclusive host of a true-crime podcast about the twenty-year-old disappearance of a local girl, receives an anonymous retainer to prove that a murder in his own town hasn't happened yet — a murder scheduled, according to a cryptic ledger hidden in the town archive's plain sight, for the anniversary week. As he decodes entries implicating the town's founding families, he realizes the ledger is a kill-list maintained across generations, and that his own podcast has been feeding its keeper fresh targets. The final entry bears Sebastian's name; the client who hired him is the ledger's current custodian, testing whether Sebastian will join the system or burn it. In the flooded quarry where the first victim was never found, Sebastian chooses exposure over belonging, broadcasting the ledger live and forcing the town — and himself — into the light.
about_author: Freya Oyelaran is a former court stenographer from coastal Maine who spent a decade transcribing small-town trials before turning to fiction. She writes about communities that keep their own ledgers, and the people who finally refuse to balance them.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. A cash-stuffed envelope arrives with one instruction: prove that Eleanor Voss will not be murdered on the anniversary of her mother's disappearance. Sebastian, who built his podcast on the old case, dismisses it as a crank — until he finds a page torn from the town archive tucked inside. Emotional beat: unease masquerading as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Towns
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. He revisits his meticulously filed research and notices gaps he never questioned: witnesses who recanted identically, dates that align across decades. His producer, Dana, pushes him toward the anniversary episode while warning him off 'conspiracy drift.' Emotional beat: the comfort of order beginning to curdle into complicity.

chapters.title: Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. In the archive's public genealogy indexes, he finds the cipher: family names whose birth and death dates encode payments, and initials matching unsolved disappearances going back a century. The ledger isn't hidden — it's maintained openly by whoever keeps the town's records. Emotional beat: vertigo as the familiar becomes monstrous.

chapters.title: Eleanor Voss
chapters.summary: POV alternating Sebastian and Eleanor. Eleanor, a young archivist and daughter of the missing woman, admits she sent the letter — she found her own name dated next year. She trusts Sebastian because his podcast kept her mother's case alive. Emotional beat: fragile alliance, two lonely people recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Founding Families
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. He confronts Judge Aldous Crane, whose name anchors the oldest entries, and is met with warm hospitality and a veiled threat — an offer to fund the podcast 'properly.' That night his studio is ransacked, but only the original files are taken. Emotional beat: the seduction and menace of institutional power.

chapters.title: What the Podcast Was For
chapters.summary: POV Dana. Dana discovers the podcast's anonymous hosting payments trace back to a Crane-family trust: the show wasn't investigating the town, it was cataloguing it — identifying who remembered too much. She must decide whether to tell Sebastian she helped build his cage. Emotional beat: guilt and the terror of losing belonging.

chapters.title: Anniversary Week
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. The town prepares its memorial festival as Eleanor goes missing and the ledger's newest ink appears: her entry moved up. Sebastian realizes the client's fee was never for investigation — it was payment for silence, and he accepted it. Emotional beat: self-reckoning; the investigator discovers he was evidence all along.

chapters.title: The Custodian
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Following the cipher to the quarry boathouse, he meets the ledger's keeper — the beloved town historian, who offers him succession: the list protects the town, she claims, by sacrificing few to save many, and every keeper was once an outsider who wanted to belong. Emotional beat: temptation framed as homecoming.

chapters.title: Quarry Water
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian and Eleanor. Eleanor, held at the quarry, escapes her bindings as Sebastian arrives; the confrontation turns violent when Crane's enforcer arrives to close both entries. Sebastian records everything rather than fight, luring the keeper into confessing the system aloud. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Last Verdict
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. He broadcasts the confession and decoded ledger live during the memorial ceremony, letting the town hear its own history read aloud; arrests follow, but so does exile — neighbors who needed the ledger's order now shun him. Eleanor leaves to find her mother's truth elsewhere; Sebastian stays, finally visible. Emotional beat: justice outside the law costs belonging, and it's worth it.
